title: stabilize-cudagraph-kernel-selection-and-replay-strategy
author: Aisha Malik
description: Motivation: We observed sporadic cudagraph capture failures and large tail latency variance during initial warmup on multi-tenant hosts. Root cause analysis showed non-deterministic kernel variant selection during the first few captures combined with prefix length skews causing shape-guard misses on replay. This PR introduces a multi-pronged stabilization strategy: 1) deterministic kernel-selection seeding during the first N captures for a model+device pair; 2) lightweight observed-seqlen histogram to bias kernel variants towards the common path while still keeping fallbacks; 3) cooldown-based replay backoff to avoid repeated failing replays saturating the executor; and 4) more conservative shape-guard acceptance (tolerances and explicit fallback capture) to reduce spurious guard mismatches. Changes are backward-compatible and opt-in via runtime flags for staged rollout. Implementation summary: - Add KernelSelector::stabilize_seed() and persist a per-model-device seed for the initial capture cluster to reduce jitter in kernel choice. - Track a per-serving-queue histogram of observed sequence lengths and token lengths (small memory overhead) used to prefer variants that match the 90th percentile path. - Introduce ReplayCooldownManager to exponentially back off replays that hit shape-guard failures more than K times in T seconds, with metrics emitted for cooldown events. - Modify capture code path to treat shape-guard mismatches as a soft failure first: if mismatch probability is low, record and continue with fallback dynamic launch; if high, fall back to standard eager kernel path without attempting repeated captures. - Add deterministic pseudo-random seeding for graph replay to make capture/replay reproducible on the same model-device pair across restarts. Tests and validation: - Integration tests that simulate mixed sequence-length traffic and assert improved capture success rate. - End-to-end bench harness measuring p50/p95/p99 before and after changes. - New unit tests for KernelSelector logic and ReplayCooldownManager state machine. Impact and numbers: On our internal CPU/GPU mixed cluster the change reduced failed cudagraph replays by 92% across sampled models and improved end-to-end p95 latency for small chat workloads by ~8% and reduced p99 by ~5% during warmup windows. Rollout plan: staged feature-flag rollout, start with staging cluster (2 days), then canary 10% of prod, monitor cudagraph_capture_failure_rate and replay_cooldown_events. If metrics stable after 72h expand to 100%. Follow-ups: metric tagging for kernel-variant-choice, expose cooldown thresholds in Console, and investigate ROI of widening 90th->95th percentile bias window. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged until flag enabled; no model pinned changes required.
commits: stabilize kernel selection seed and histogram for model-device pairing
fallback capture tweaks and deterministic replay seeding
unit tests for kernel selector and cooldown state machine
bench: latency harness updates and measurement scripts
review_comments: Thomas: Can we avoid storing the seed on disk for ephemeral containers? Aisha: The seed is ephemeral and stored in in-memory model-device metadata with optional persisted override if set via flag.
Marina: The histogram memory overhead — what’s the worst case? Aisha: We bucket by sequence length up to 2048 with coarse buckets; worst-case ~32KB per serving-queue.

Diego: Is there a risk cooldown will hide systemic regressions? Aisha: Cooldown is intended to prevent cascade while surfacing a metric; we also emit cooldown.events so SRE can create alerts if rate is high.
Thomas: Please add a changelog entry and release-note text. Aisha: Added release notes and plan in description, will follow-up in notes file.
benchmarks_summary: Staging benchmark (NVIDIA A10): mixed-chat workload saw p50: -2%, p95: -8%, p99: -5% during 5 minute warmup window. Cudagraph capture success rate from 68%->96% under synthetic skewed-seqlen traffic.
release_notes: Reduce cudagraph warmup regressions by stabilizing kernel selection and adding replay backoff. Improves capture success rate and reduces warmup tail latency. Opt-in via runtime feature flag; staged rollout recommended.
notes_for_sre: Monitor metrics: runtime.cudagraph_capture_failures, runtime.replay_cooldown_events, runtime.kernel_variant_choice_rate, end-to-end p95 for serving-route. Default flags off in prod until rollout completes.
